final_candidates.decision_summary: R1699 is a critical Arg in the second BRCT repeat; R1699W is a known deleterious variant that disrupts the phosphopeptide-binding interface and abolishes tumor-suppressor function while the domain remains largely folded.
M1775 packs in the BRCT hydrophobic core; M1775R destabilizes the BRCT interaction surface and impairs BACH1/ABL1 binding and transcriptional activity without fully unfolding the protein.
K1702 contributes to the BRCT phosphopeptide-binding pocket; a charge-reversal K1702E should strongly reduce binding affinity with only modest impact on folding due to surface exposure.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 is stable and additional rounds without external evidence would not improve it.

history.rationale: BRCT-domain cancer-associated mutation that abolishes phospho-peptide binding of BRCA1 to Abraxas/CtIP/MERIT40 while leaving the BRCT fold largely intact.

R1699 is a critical Arg in the second BRCT repeat of BRCA1; the R1699W founder variant disrupts BRCT fold/phosphopeptide-binding interface and abolishes tumor-suppressor function while remaining expressible. Structural perturbation is localized and the domain remains largely folded.
Classic pathogenic BRCT mutation disrupting the phosphoserine-binding pocket without grossly destabilizing overall folding.

M1775 packs in the BRCT hydrophobic core; M1775R is a classic deleterious missense variant that destabilizes the BRCT-phosphopeptide binding surface without fully unfolding the protein. Strong loss-of-function with partial folding retention.
Reverses charge at a key BRCT pocket lysine that coordinates the phosphopeptide phosphate, abolishing interactions with repair-complex partners.

K1702 contributes to the BRCT phosphopeptide-binding pocket and BRCT-repeat interaction; charge-reversal to Glu should impair BACH1/ABL1 binding and transcriptional activity. Folding impact is modest because it is a surface-exposed charge change.
RING-domain zinc-coordinating cysteine mutation that cripples BARD1 heterodimerization/E3 ligase activity, though it may partly perturb RING fold.

C61 is a zinc-coordinating residue in the RING domain; C61G disrupts E3 ubiquitin ligase activity but risks local misfolding of the RING domain. Retained but demoted due to folding-preservation concern.
Another zinc-ligating cysteine in the RING domain whose substitution impairs E3 ubiquitin-ligase tumor-suppressor function.
C39 is also a RING zinc ligand; substituting a bulky Tyr likely destabilizes the zinc-binding fold more than C61G, conflicting with the folding-preservation goal.

rejection.reason: C39 is also a RING zinc ligand; substituting a bulky Tyr likely destabilizes the zinc-binding fold more than C61G, conflicting with the folding-preservation goal.

history.rationale: BRCT-domain residue at the interaction interface; substitution to bulky Phe blocks phospho-peptide partner binding with modest folding impact.
S1655 is an unvalidated surface position in the linker/BRCT region with weak mechanistic rationale for functional ablation; a bulky Phe may perturb structure with uncertain functional gain.

rejection.reason: S1655 is an unvalidated surface position in the linker/BRCT region with weak mechanistic rationale for functional ablation; a bulky Phe may perturb structure with uncertain functional gain.

history.rationale: BRCT pocket residue; a Lys substitution introduces conflicting positive charge into the phosphate-binding site, reducing partner binding.
T1691K lacks strong functional annotation and an added positive charge near the BRCT core has unpredictable consequences; low confidence in functional ablation.

rejection.reason: T1691K lacks strong functional annotation and an added positive charge near the BRCT core has unpredictable consequences; low confidence in functional ablation.

history.rationale: RING-domain cysteine candidate (verify WT identity) whose disruption could abolish ligase function while retaining the BRCT region.
C64 is a RING zinc ligand; C64Y likely both ablates function and misfolds the RING domain, failing the folding constraint worse than C61G.

rejection.reason: C64 is a RING zinc ligand; C64Y likely both ablates function and misfolds the RING domain, failing the folding constraint worse than C61G.
